{{Technical|date=December 2021}}
'''Shearer's inequality''' or also Shearer's lemma, in [[mathematics]], is an inequality in [[information theory]] relating the [[Entropy (information theory)|entropy]] of a set of variables to the entropies of a collection of subsets. It is named for mathematician [[James B. Shearer]].

Concretely, it states that if ''X''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''X''<sub>''d''</sub> are [[random variable]]s and ''S''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''S''<sub>''n''</sub> are subsets of {1,&nbsp;2,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''d''} such that every integer between 1 and ''d'' lies in at least ''r'' of these subsets, then

: <math> H[(X_1,\dots,X_d)] \leq \frac{1}{r}\sum_{i=1}^n H[(X_j)_{j\in S_i}]</math>

where <math>H</math> is entropy and <math> (X_{j})_{j\in S_{i}}</math> is the [[Cartesian product]] of random variables <math>X_{j}</math> with indices ''j'' in <math>S_{i}</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Chung|first1=F.R.K.|last2=Graham|first2=R.L.|author-link2=Ronald Graham|last3=Frankl|first3=P.|last4=Shearer|first4=J.B.|title=Some Intersection Theorems for Ordered Sets and Graphs|journal=J. Comb. Theory A|date=1986|volume=43|pages=23–37|doi=10.1016/0097-3165(86)90019-1|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The inequality generalizes the [[Entropy_(information_theory)#Alternative_characterization_via_additivity_and_subadditivity|subadditivity property of entropy]], which can be recovered by taking <math>S_i = \{i\}</math> for <math>i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}</math>.<ref name="Galvin2014">{{cite arXiv|last=Galvin|first=David|date=2014-06-30|title=Three tutorial lectures on entropy and counting|class=math.CO|eprint=1406.7872}}</ref>

== Combinatorial version ==
Let <math>\mathcal{F}</math> be a family of subsets of <math>[n]</math> (possibly with repeats) with each <math>i\in [n]</math> included in at least <math>t</math> members of <math>\mathcal{F}</math>. Let <math>\mathcal{A}</math> be another set of subsets of <math>[n]</math>. Then

: <math> \mathcal |\mathcal{A}|\leq \prod_{F\in \mathcal{F}}|\operatorname{trace}_{F}(\mathcal{A})|^{1/t}</math>

where <math> \operatorname{trace}_{F}(\mathcal{A})=\{A\cap F:A\in\mathcal{A}\}</math> the set of possible intersections of elements of <math> \mathcal{A}</math> with <math> F</math>.<ref name="Galvin2014" />
